v.title: Celentano’s Clean Sheet Shocks Shield‑Winners Nashville
v.excerpt: Celentano’s six saves give Cincinnati a 1‑0 win over Shield‑winners Nashville, igniting a best‑of‑three MLS playoff series.
v.body:
## Quick take
Roman Celentano’s six‑save masterpiece gave FC Cincinnati a 1‑0 win over Shield‑winners Nashville, sparking a 1‑0 lead in a best‑of‑three MLS Cup Play‑off series.

## What happened
The match opened with a bizarre early own goal from Nashville’s midfielder, handing Cincinnati the advantage before the first half even finished. Celentano, who has already posted four clean sheets this season, stood firm as Nashville’s relentless attacks turned into a flurry of chances. He made a series of acrobatic saves, including a fingertip stop on a low cross and a diving block on a looping shot from Nashville’s striker.

Despite the early setback, Nashville pressed hard. Their midfield tried to force a corner, but Celentano’s quick reflexes denied every attempt. The game stayed tight, with both sides exchanging possession but failing to convert. The 1‑0 scoreline was sealed when Cincinnati’s defender, after a defensive error, inadvertently headed the ball into his own net, cementing the victory.

## Why it matters
- **Celentano’s form signals a defensive renaissance for Cincinnati**: With a clean sheet streak that rivals some of the league’s top clubs, the goalkeeper is proving that the team can compete with any opponent, including the Shield‑winners Nashville.
- **The early own goal highlights Nashville’s vulnerability**: A single defensive lapse cost them the game, and in a best‑of‑three series, momentum swings can be decisive. Barcelona fans will note how crucial composure is when facing high‑pressure matches.
- **The result reshapes the MLS Cup narrative**: Cincinnati’s comeback win suggests that the underdog can challenge the league’s elite. For Barcelona, it serves as a reminder that even the best teams can stumble if they let early mistakes dictate the pace.

## What's next
The series shifts to Nashville’s home turf. Watch Celentano’s response to the pressure—will he maintain his clean‑sheet streak or falter under the bright lights? Also, keep an eye on Nashville’s defensive strategy; they’ll need to tighten up to avoid another early own goal. The next match will decide whether Cincinnati can capitalize on this momentum and edge closer to the MLS Cup, or if Nashville will rally and level the series.
